tax-equivalent-yield.summary: Tax-equivalent yield answers a simple question: what taxable annual yield would match your tax-exempt income after tax? Enter both yields and the tax rates that apply to this interest. Use the same annual yield basis for both options. This comparison is for an ordinary taxable account. Equal after-tax income does not mean equal investment risk.
tax-equivalent-yield.scope: You enter the marginal tax rates: the rates on the next dollar of interest. The tool assumes the exempt option qualifies for federal tax exemption. Choose whether state and local taxes apply to it. Enter any extra investment-income tax rate yourself. The tool adds the entered rates without adjusting for tax deductions. It does not choose a tax bracket or check exemption eligibility. It does not model alternative minimum tax (AMT), eligibility for Net Investment Income Tax (NIIT), partly exempt fund payments, capital gains or retirement accounts.

examples.title: Four percent exempt equals five percent taxable at a 20% rate
examples.inputs: Invest $10,000. The exempt annual yield is 4%, with no federal, state or local tax. The taxable annual yield is 5%. Its combined marginal tax rate is 20%.
steps: Each option earns $400 a year after tax on $10,000.
examples.answer: The required taxable yield is 5%. Both options earn the same after-tax income, so the income advantage is $0.

questions.question: Which tax rate should I enter?
questions.answer: Use the rates that apply to the next dollar of this interest income. These are marginal rates, not your average tax rate. The tool adds federal, state, local and any extra investment-income tax rate you enter. It does not select tax brackets or adjust for deductions. It also does not check whether Net Investment Income Tax (NIIT) applies to you.

questions.question: Are all municipal bonds completely tax-free?
questions.answer: No. This tool assumes the bond qualifies for federal tax exemption. You must choose its state and local tax treatment. Out-of-state interest may be taxable. Fund payments may be only partly exempt. Some private-activity bonds can trigger alternative minimum tax (AMT). Capital gains need a separate calculation. Choosing Exempt does not prove that you qualify.

questions.question: Can I compare this with a Treasury bill or CD?
questions.answer: Yes, if you use the same annual yield basis and check each tax rule. This form applies all entered rates to the taxable option. Treasury bill interest is subject to federal tax but exempt from state and local tax. To compare a fully exempt municipal bond with a Treasury bill, set state and local rates to zero. This form cannot model a state-taxed municipal bond against a state-exempt Treasury bill. That case needs separate state tax rates for each investment.

questions.question: Does the sensitivity table show current tax brackets?
questions.answer: No. The table tests different combined tax rates for the taxable option. The exempt option keeps the tax treatment you selected. These are comparison scenarios, not current federal or state tax brackets.

treasury-bill.summary: A Treasury bill pays its face value at maturity; discount interest is the difference from its purchase price. This calculator separates bank discount rate, return on the actual purchase cost, simple annualization and hypothetical effective annual yield. Fees and your federal tax assumptions are reported separately.
treasury-bill.scope: Ordinary U.S. Treasury bill held to maturity, positive discount/par price and1..366 whole days. Quotes are manual assumptions, not live auction data. No official auction Investment Rate, early-sale valuation, investment ladder, full tax-basis/accrual treatment or retirement-account model.

examples.title: TreasuryDirect discount-pricing example
examples.inputs: Face$1,000;182 days; bank discount rate0.145%; no fee/tax in this illustration.
steps: Unrounded interest =$0.7330555556. Actual broker/auction rounding may differ.

examples.title: Quoted price separates gross profit from fee and tax
examples.inputs: $10,000 face bought at$98 per$100 face;91 days; fee$10; federal marginal tax24%.
steps: Purchase price =10,000×98/100=$9,800; purchase cash including fee =$9,810.
Gross discount interest =$200; estimated federal tax =$48.
examples.answer: Net maturity profit after entered fee and estimated tax is$142.

expected.label: Net profit at maturity after fee and tax

questions.question: Which rate goes in Quoted bank discount rate?
questions.answer: Use a quote explicitly expressed as a bank discount rate. Its denominator is face value and its year basis is360 days. Do not enter a broker Investment Rate, APY or simple annualized yield as a bank discount quote. If you know the price, use Yield from Purchase Price instead.

questions.question: Why is simple annualized yield not the official Treasury Investment Rate?
questions.answer: The displayed simple annualized yield scales return on price by365 or366 divided by holding days. Official auction and broker bond-equivalent conventions can differ, especially for longer bills. This calculator deliberately labels its own convention and does not claim official Investment Rate output.

questions.question: Is the effective annual yield guaranteed?
questions.answer: No. It assumes reinvestment repeatedly at the same holding-period return across a full year. Bills pay at maturity, and future auction rates are unknown. It is a mathematical comparison figure, not an accrued daily payout or guaranteed annual return.

questions.question: How are federal tax and state taxes handled?
questions.answer: The tool estimates federal tax plus an entered effective surtax on positive gross discount interest. Bill interest is exempt from state/local income tax. Fees reduce net profit but are not deducted from the estimated tax base; secondary-sale gains, accrual rules and investor-specific basis adjustments are excluded.

questions.question: Can I enter a 13-week or 26-week term?
questions.answer: Use91 or182 days for nominal13- or26-week examples, or enter the actual settlement-to-maturity day count. Common nominal week terms are4,6,8,13,17,26 and52 weeks; holidays and actual issue/maturity dates can affect the correct days. A52-week shortcut is364 days, not automatically365.
